strings: Alliance Relations is an introductory quest offered by Craven Drok in Orgrimmar. It directs seasoned Horde adventurers to seek out Keldran, a mystic operating quietly near the city's western exit. The task opens a conversation about the delicate, behind-the-scenes diplomacy and intelligence work required to maintain Thrall's fragile peace with the Alliance.

While many orcs favor brute strength and straightforward conquest, Warchief Thrall understands that endless war with the Alliance would ruin his young nation. Having grown up in human captivity, Thrall learned the subtle nuances of human statecraft and military strategy. Craven Drok notices warriors and champions who might possess the patience for a more nuanced approach, directing them to look beyond raw force.

Tucked away near the western gates of Orgrimmar sits the humble dwelling of Keldran, a practitioner of magic and covert arts. Unlike the boisterous warriors drinking in the Valley of Strength, Keldran deals in appearances, perception, and statecraft. He seeks operatives capable of exercising discretion on behalf of the Warchief, navigating the tense standoff between the Horde and its bitter rivals.

Alliance Relations is a Horde assignment dispatched from Orgrimmar to Desolace to prevent dangerous political fallout. With the Alliance pushing deeper into central Kalimdor, the Horde moves proactively to purge regional Burning Legion forces before rivals can accuse Thrall's people of renewed demonic corruption.

As Alliance scouts and expeditions venture across Kalimdor, Horde leadership faces a delicate diplomatic threat. The presence of demonic remnants scattered across central Kalimdor risks confirming old prejudices that the orcs and their allies remain in league with the Burning Legion. Acting with Warchief Thrall's sanction, Keldran in Orgrimmar oversees targeted operations to ensure these demonic remnants are wiped out before hostile Alliance factions can twist their presence into justification for war.

Carrying orders southward requires passing through the Charred Vale of the Stonetalon Mountains down into the bleak expanse of Desolace. There, just north of the vast Kodo Graveyard, lies Ghost Walker Post. Horde agents like Takata Steelblade monitor the desolate wilderness, navigating both the rampant centaur tribes and the pervasive demonic corruption that threatens to overrun the region.

Takata Steelblade regards the assignment with grim pragmatism. Though wiping out the local demons inevitably relieves pressure on the violent native centaur tribes and even assists the Horde's resident warlocks, the duty takes precedence. Eliminating the Burning Legion's footholds serves the broader security of the Horde, regardless of who else might profit from the culling.

Messenger to Westfall is a diplomatic errand that carries Gryan Stoutmantle's sober reply from Sentinel Hill back to Magistrate Solomon in Lakeshire. Solomon, beleaguered by local threats in Redridge, sought military reinforcement from the People's Militia, only to learn that Westfall is equally forsaken by the crown.

Magistrate Solomon of Lakeshire found himself facing mounting crises in the Redridge Mountains without the backing of Stormwind's royal garrison. Looking across the southern regions of the kingdom for allies, he reached out to Gryan Stoutmantle, commander of the People's Militia in Westfall. Solomon hoped the organized volunteer force securing Sentinel Hill might spare troops to bolster Lakeshire's defenses, unaware of the grim realities gripping the western plains.

Gryan Stoutmantle's response is an unambiguous, heavy-hearted refusal. Westfall is consumed by its own desperate war against the Defias Brotherhood and marauding gnolls, a struggle made necessary only because the House of Nobles and the crown have abandoned their breadbasket. Stoutmantle makes clear that the People's Militia exists out of sheer survival; they are losing good men daily and cannot spare a single fighter to rescue Redridge.

Returning Stoutmantle's reply to Lakeshire shatters Solomon's illusions. The Magistrate realizes that the kingdom's frontier territories share the same abandonment, with local magistrates and citizen militias left to fend for themselves while the Stormwind Army remains inexplicably withheld. This disappointment drives Solomon to look south, setting his sights on Darkshire in Duskwood for aid.

"Seeking the Kor Gem" is an Alliance paladin quest that sends an initiate deep into the ancient ruins of northern Kalimdor. Directed by the night elf Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine, paladins venture into Blackfathom Deeps to wrest a potent Kor gem from the naga who corrupt it. The retrieved stone serves as a key material in Jordan Stilwell's craft.

When paladins in training seek the materials needed by the human smith Jordan Stilwell, their journey crosses continental borders to Darkshore. There, at Auberdine, Thundris Windweaver remembers the blacksmith with respect. Despite the natural aloofness of the night elves and the transgressions of certain fallen human figures, Thundris holds faith in paladins pursuing a righteous path and willingly reveals where such ancient gems are found.

The search leads directly to the subterranean temple complex of Blackfathom Deeps along the foggy northwestern coast of Ashenvale. Inhabited by Twilight's Hammer cultists and treacherous sea-dwellers, the watery depths are also home to naga priestesses who channel foul magic through ancient Kor gems. A paladin must brave these dark halls, defeat the sorceresses, and secure a gem steeped in serpentine malice.

Returning a corrupted Kor gem to Thundris Windweaver reveals the true purpose of seeking out an elven mystic. While the naga imbue the gem with raw magical potency, their enchantments twist it toward evil. Before Jordan Stilwell can forge it into a holy weapon, Thundris must excise the darkness, ensuring its power remains pure and stable for the sacred smithing ritual ahead.

The Rethban Gauntlet is an eccentric endurance trial devised by the dwarven brewer Yorus Barleybrew in Lakeshire. Challengers must drink a potent swig of his family's fiery Barleybrew Scalder and sprint north into the gnoll-infested Rethban Caverns and back before an hour elapses.

In the town of Lakeshire, where grim talk of gnoll raids and missing town guards usually dominates the inn, the dwarf Yorus Barleybrew brings a distinctly dwarven flavor of entertainment. His self-styled challenge, the Rethban Gauntlet, tests an adventurer's mettle, speed, and liver all at once. Participants are required to down a draught of his family's signature concoction, Barleybrew Scalder, right before setting off on foot toward the northern foothills.

The trial is far more perilous than a simple drunken footrace. Between Lakeshire and the destination lies Redridge territory teeming with aggressive Redridge gnolls. To successfully complete the gauntlet, the runner must fight or slip past the packs, reach the first fork inside the dark tunnels of Rethban Caverns, and hustle back to Yorus within an hour—all while battling the overwhelming, staggering effects of the fiery dwarven alcohol.
